syllabusTopics: Saturated hydrocarbons (Alkanes): preparation from haloalkanes (reduction and Wurtz reaction), decarboxylation, catalytic hydrogenation of alkene and alkyne
Chemical properties of alkanes: substitution reactions (halogenation, nitration and sulphonation only), oxidation of ethane
Unsaturated hydrocarbons (Alkenes): preparation by dehydration of alcohol, dehydrohalogenation, catalytic hydrogenation of alkyne
Chemical properties of alkenes: addition reaction with HX (Markovnikov's addition and peroxide effect), H2O, O3, H2SO4 only
Alkynes: preparation from carbon and hydrogen, 1,2-dibromoethane, chloroform/iodoform only
Chemical properties of alkynes: addition reaction with H2, HX, H2O; acidic nature (action with sodium, ammoniacal AgNO3 and ammoniacal Cu2Cl2)
Test of unsaturation (ethene and ethyne): bromine water test and Baeyer's test
Comparative studies of physical properties of alkane, alkene and alkyne
Kolbe's electrolysis methods for the preparation of alkanes, alkenes and alkynes

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The alkene π bond invites electrophiles. **HX adds by Markovnikov's rule** — the negative part lands on the carbon with **fewer hydrogens**, because H⁺ first creates the **more stable carbocation** (propene + HBr → **2-bromopropane**).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - CH₃–CH=CH₂ + HBr → CH₃–CHBr–CH₃ (Markovnikov) - CH₃–CH=CH₂ + HBr (ROOR) → CH₃–CH₂–CH₂Br - CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O (H₂SO₄) → CH₃CH₂OH - CH₂=CH₂ + O₃ → ozonide → 2 HCHO (Zn/H₂O); CH₃CH=CHCH₃ → 2 CH₃CHO

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "Markovnikov's rule: the negative part of the addendum attaches to the alkene carbon bearing fewer hydrogens; peroxides reverse this for HBr via a radical mechanism."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***HBr's private quirk*** — of the four hydrogen halides only HBr flips in peroxides: Cl· adds too fast to be selective, I· too weak to sustain the chain — bond energetics police the exception.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The π Bond Under Attack A π bond is an exposed electron cloud — every electrophile wants it. Alkene chemistry is **electrophilic addition**: HX, H₂O, H₂SO₄ and O₃ all add across the double bond, with **Markovnikov's rule** and the **peroxide effect** deciding which carbon gets which fragment.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Addition of HX and Markovnikov's rule - **CH₃–CH=CH₂ + HBr → CH₃–CHBr–CH₃** (2-bromopropane, major). - **Markovnikov's rule:** the **negative part** of the addendum attaches to the carbon with **fewer hydrogens**; equivalently H⁺ goes to the carbon already holding more H. - Reason: the more stable **carbocation** (3° > 2° > 1°) forms on the more substituted carbon.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Markovnikov: X to H-poor C (2-bromopropane). Peroxide + HBr: reverse (1-bromopropane). Ozonolysis: terminal C → HCHO; symmetrical internal → 2 same carbonyls. Hydration: H2SO4 then water → alcohol.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Whoever forms the stabler intermediate wins: Markovnikov is carbocation stability in disguise, and the peroxide effect is radical stability pulling the other way.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Alkene chemistry = electrophilic addition. HX: Markovnikov's rule — negative part (X-) goes to the carbon with FEWER H; via the more stable carbocation; CH3CH=CH2 + HBr -> CH3CHBrCH3 (2-bromopropane).…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Ozonolysis is molecular archaeology: cleave the alkene, read the carbonyl fragments, and the position of the original double bond is reconstructed exactly.

rows.text: ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | **Markovnikov's rule** | Negative addendum goes to the C with fewer H (via the stabler carbocation) | propene + HBr → 2-bromopropane | | **Peroxide effect** | Radical anti-Markovnikov addition, HBr only | propene + HBr/ROOR → 1-bromopropane | | **Ozonolysis** | O₃ addition then Zn/H₂O cleavage…  ·  ## 4. Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 The carbocation is the hinge - H⁺ adds first (electrophilic), creating a carbocation; the more substituted cation forms preferentially, and the anion then attacks it. Every Markovnikov question is a carbocation-stability question.…  ·  ## 5. Comparison Tables **Markovnikov vs peroxide (Kharasch) addition** | Basis | Markovnikov | Peroxide effect | |---|---|---| | mechanism | ionic (carbocation) | free-radical | | condition | normal | peroxides, HBr only | | H goes to | C with more H | C with fewer H | | Br goes to | C with fewer H | C with more H | | propene + HBr | 2-bromopropane | 1-bromopropane |

Common Confusions **The rule speaks of the negative part:** it is Br⁻ that goes to the H-poor carbon — students misplace the H instead.  ·  **Peroxide effect is HBr-only:** writing it for HCl or HI is a classic error — bond energetics forbid the chain.
